title: Death toll from devastating floods in China and Nepal surpasses 1,000 - Al Jazeera
description: Death toll from devastating floods in China and Nepal surpasses 1,000  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
The death toll from catastrophic flooding in Nepal and China has reached 1,019, and more than 4,400 people remain missing as rescue crews work to reach communities cut off by the disaster.

In an update on Tuesday, Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) increased the number of deaths from 987 to 1,003, with 3,916 people missing, including 583 foreigners.

Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 people still missing, including 261 foreigners, in their most recent update on Sunday.

The disaster hit on August 26 , beginning with a chain of events high in the Himalayas, when a glacial collapse sent large amounts of rock, ice, and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream.

Scientists studying satellite imagery said the collapse appears to have involved the failure of bedrock beneath a glacier.

Hundreds of workers are feared to be trapped in tunnels at several devastated hydropower stations in Nepal that have become the focus of rescue efforts.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah said 279 workers had been rescued from hydropower projects so far, where authorities had initially estimated that more than 900 people were missing.

More than 11,000 people have been rescued across the affected region, and power and communication lines have been restored in some areas, he added.

“Thousands of citizens have lost their homes, families, loved ones, and property,” Shah said on social media.

“The government understands the immense pain they are enduring. The path ahead is to support them through this suffering and help them return to normal life through rehabilitation.”

Advertisement

Rescue teams had managed to restore road networks to Nuwakot, one of the worst-affected districts, facilitating rescue operations and the distribution of relief material, Shah said.

Aid arrives in Nepal

Police official Bipin Regmi said a search team recovered 24 bodies from a house in Betrabati village in Nuwakot district.

“We are reaching new areas and recovering bodies,” Regmi told the Reuters news agency.

Aid worth more than $42m has poured into the country after the disaster, Shah said, and the government expects the contributions to increase.

Neighbours India and China are helping with rescue efforts, including building Bailey bridges to reach remote affected areas.

Pictures and videos shared by rescue teams showed earth-moving equipment digging and shovelling mud and rocks under lights in the dark of the night as workers watched.

Soldiers used torchlight in a big pit they had created to look for space to get into one tunnel.

There has been a boom in hydropower projects in Nepal since the turn of the century, as the mountainous country sought to take advantage of its Himalayan water resources to address chronic domestic power shortages and exploit prospects for selling electricity to its southern neighbour, India.

Hydropower projects in Nepal’s mountains need tunnels to carry water through the steep terrain, allowing developers to exploit the sharp elevation drop between Himalayan rivers and powerhouses to generate electricity.

title: They were building infrastructure in Nepal. Their families in China want to know what happened to them - CNN
description: They were building infrastructure in Nepal. Their families in China want to know what happened to them  CNN
publisher.title: CNN
full_article:
Beijing —

She kept calling and calling – countless times – but her husband never picked up.

The woman, who CNN has given the pseudonym Lili, said her husband had spoken with a friend at 8:27am on Wednesday. That was roughly 10 minutes before an enormous landslide careened down a mountain in Nepal, generating an explosive flood wave that ripped through a border area with China and continued into Nepal.

Lili hasn’t heard from her husband, who was working on a Chinese construction project in the South Asian country, since.

Hers is one of many families across China desperate for information about loved ones who were in the area when disaster struck, including dozens of Chinese nationals who are believed to have been working across the border in Nepal.

Now, these families are wondering whether rescue efforts in Nepal are reaching their loved ones – and are urgently calling for more proactive updates on the progress of those efforts from within China.

Video Ad Feedback Rescuers up against the clock to try and find survivors in Nepal tunnels 3:03 • Source: CNN Rescuers up against the clock to try and find survivors in Nepal tunnels 3:03

Several family members of such workers traveled to Lhasa, the capital of China’s Tibetan Autonomous Region, on Monday to seek more information from the state-backed construction firm employing their relatives – and to urge the company to step up rescue efforts and share more information. Families are also asking for local officials in Tibet to help expedite rescue efforts at project sites in Nepal, according to a draft letter to authorities seen by CNN.

More than 1,000 people have been confirmed dead and thousands remain missing after Wednesday’s catastrophe, according to authorities in both China and Nepal. Families from both countries – and around the world – are desperate for news of loved ones in the area, which was also a popular route for international tourists.

While updates on the numbers of those rescued or confirmed dead have been frequently released on the Nepal side, information has moved much more slowly coming out of China – prompting questions about transparency. Beijing has defended the release of information from its remote disaster area as open and timely.

Inside China, news coverage in the country’s tightly controlled media environment has been dominated by state media reports and focused on the efforts of emergency responders at the China-Nepal border area. The experiences of the Chinese families, who are among those waiting for news, have had limited visibility.

“Our family is in anguish,” Lili told CNN, adding that her children had stayed in their bedrooms since they learned that their father was missing. CNN is using pseudonyms in order to protect the families’ identities due to the sensitivities of speaking to foreign media.

Lili’s husband, who is in his fifties, had been working on the reconstruction of Nepal’s Syabrubesi-Rasuwagadhi highway, a road stretching through part of northern Nepal to the border with China. Its construction is run by Chinese state-backed engineering firm Tibet Tianlu Company – one of several Chinese firms participating in infrastructure projects across Nepal.

After the disaster struck, the company deployed its specialists as well as relief supplies and heavy machinery, while its leadership visited the hard-hit Gyirong port area in Tibet, where rescue efforts are underway, Tibet Tianlu Company said in online statements.

But Lili and family members of other workers on that project worry that rescue efforts are being hindered by the location of the project – in Nepal, but close to the Chinese border.

“It’s still the families themselves who are organizing and trying to get the rescue efforts moving — going to talk to the (company) leaders, asking them to coordinate with the Nepali government,” Lili said.

The sister of another worker on the same highway project told CNN that she believes Nepali rescue workers had not yet been able to reach the area where the project is located. “We haven’t received any information at all … our whole family is extremely worried,” she said.

The launch ceremony of the Syaphrubesi-Rasuwagadi Highway Repair and Improvement Project in Nepal, in 2019. The project is constructed by Lhasa-based Tibet Tianlu Company Limited. Tibet Tianlu Company Limited

In a draft letter addressed to government officials in Tibet seen by CNN, relatives of 24 of the workers on the highway project expressed concern of a gap in “cross-border rescue efforts.”

“Local rescue resources and manpower in Nepal are severely limited and unable to reach the core area to conduct searches. On our side, restrictions arising from the border mean that Chinese rescuers are temporarily unable to cross into the site to carry out rescue operations directly,” said the letter, which CNN has not confirmed was delivered to officials.

“We sincerely ask you to understand the families’ anguish… and take concrete steps to get rescue operations underway,” it said. The families also called for authorities to require the company to establish a regular update mechanism for the progress of search and rescue operations, so that “information is transparent and timely.”

When reached by phone, a person from Tibet Tianlu’s Board Secretary Office said a team had been set up to handle the situation following the disaster and the company was in touch with families that had arrived at their offices on Monday. When asked about any plans for company rescue efforts on the Nepal side, the person said she “hadn’t received any information” about this.

Private and military helicopters are deployed to rescue people stranded in areas cut off by flash flooding in Nepal's Nuwakot district on Monday. Rajesh Kumar Singh/AP

Cross-border disaster

Around 100 Chinese nationals are unaccounted for in the disaster-affected area on the Nepal side, according to China’s Foreign Ministry. They are among what Nepali authorities said are more than 500 foreign nationals missing in country overall as of Monday night.

China’s Foreign Ministry on Monday said the country was “making every effort to search for and rescue people reported missing both in China and abroad.” All Chinese nationals who had been reached in the disaster zone in Nepal had been safely evacuated, it added, without giving specific number.

Chinese workers, as well as official lenders and construction firms, have played a key role in the build-out of Nepal’s roads, hydropower and other projects in recent years, including under the auspices of Chinese leader Xi Jinping’s flagship Belt and Road global infrastructure drive.

Since the disaster, family members of workers from at least three projects in Nepal, including two hydropower projects, have been in touch with one another, CNN has learned, exchanging information and concerns online – as they await official information.

Rescue workers take part in an operation near the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A Hydropower Project, following deadly flash floods and mudslide in Rasuwa, Nepal. Nepal Prime Minister's Office/Handout/Reuters

Among them, a man in his 20s CNN is calling Jun said his father had been working at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydroelectric Project in Nepal. The project is one of roughly a dozen hydropower facilities that have become a focal point for rescue efforts.

More than 500 workers remained missing at Upper Trishuli-1 as of the latest update from the Independent Power Producers Association Nepal. The project is being built by a Korean engineering firm, with a subsidiary of Chinese state-backed energy giant PowerChina also involved.

“What I really can’t understand is why Chinese rescue teams aren’t going over to the Nepalese side to help search for our Chinese nationals,” Jun said.

China has sent emergency aid supplies to Nepal and is sharing satellite and hydrological data to aid rescue efforts, as well as providing assistance with DNA identification. Over the weekend, it dispatched nine rescue tunnel experts to the country to advise on efforts to locate workers that may be trapped in hydropower project tunnels.

Nepali Army/ Nepal National Mountain Guide Association

But the lack of information is agonizing for family members like Jun, who said he had last spoken with his father, who is in his forties, during a regular family video call earlier this month.

When the mudslide struck on August 26, Jun and his family didn’t pay much attention to the news until the following day, he said, when a labor agency called to tell them that his father went missing. Jun then found his father could no longer be reached by phone.

When China for the first time on Sunday opened up two dedicated hotlines for Chinese families seeking information, Jun said he called multiple times, but the line was always busy. He’d already been in touch with the Chinese embassy in Nepal and the hydropower project manager but hasn’t been able to get information about his father’s whereabouts.

He said he wants to know the status of the search efforts – “it’s already been such a long time, right? It’s already… it’s the sixth day already,” he said Monday.

A ‘timely manner’

That painful count is also being done by families of those who were believed to be at Gyirong port in China when it was hit by a wall of floodwaters on Wednesday morning.

The impact obliterated buildings there. No survivors have been reported found since rescue workers arrived Friday afternoon at the port, according to accounts from rescue workers cited by state media.

A little girl, covering her face, crouched down in front of dozens of locals gathering at the front line of the disaster-hit area in Gyirong County, Tibet on August 30, 2026. Tibet Radio and Television Station

Updates about the missing have been slow to emerge from the area, which cannot be reached by road. The risk of additional flooding and the fact that the area is now covered by thick mud are factors impacting the speed of rescue and recovery efforts there. Information about the area has been dominated by reports from state media, in addition to official government updates.

That’s part of a usual playbook by Chinese authorities who look to closely control information flows and ensure data confirmation ahead of its release – part of efforts both to crack down on fake reports and shape public opinion.

According to China’s latest update from Sunday, there were 16 dead and 546 people missing on its side of the border. More than 250 foreigners are among the missing, local authorities in Tibet said. Chinese authorities have released new figures on the confirmed dead and missing five times since the disaster, as of Tuesday morning.

Independent aid groups are not involved in operations, while foreign journalists are restricted from Tibet without special permissions. CNN is also aware of comments from journalists from outlets that are not China’s national-level official media suggesting they have been barred from reporting in Tibet.

Reuters

Censors have been keeping close watch on online platforms, removing disaster-related videos posted by ordinary users and reprimanding at least a dozen people authorities accused of spreading fake news about the scale of the disaster. During major national incidents, the Chinese government is widely seen as swift to crack down on any forms of dissent or organized efforts to respond or share information outside official channels.

In response to a question about assertions that China was not being forthcoming about the scale of the disaster within its borders, a spokesperson for China’s Foreign Ministry said on Thursday China has been “releasing information openly, transparently and in a timely manner.”

But for family members of those who were working in Gyirong port – as with those waiting for information from Nepal – the wait for confirmation of what happened is interminable. Some have taken to social media in recent days to call out for information from any other sources.

“Seeking help from locals at Gyirong port,” one person posted on the social media platform RedNote last week. “My cousin, who serves as a border guard there, has been out of contact. What should we do? He has two children at home.”

KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — In the days since Tsering Gelbu Lama’s wife was swept away by devastating floods along the Nepal-Tibet border, he hasn’t managed to tell his 4-year-old daughter that her mother is dead.

Lama wiped away tears as he sat on the floor of a Buddhist monastery turned makeshift shelter for hundreds of others evacuated from remote villages to the capital, Kathmandu.

“I don’t know how I will pass on our culture to her,” he said as he coaxed a spoonful of rice into her mouth.

For Lama and a rising number of others displaced by the floods, the losses go beyond homes and belongings. Communities whose culture and practices, often tied to ancestral land, are eroding as young people leave for the city now worry if their sacred traditions can be preserved.

“We’ve become homeless not only because we’ve lost our land — we’ve become homeless with our culture and tradition,” said Tsering Sherpa, 36, from Rasuwa, as he sat on the monastery steps.

Rasuwa, a district in the Himalayas along the Nepal-Tibet border, is known for its distinct Buddhist culture and Indigenous communities. The Tamang Heritage Trail has become a popular trekking route for tourists looking to see Tibetan Buddhist culture.

title: 'No hollow or empty space': A drone operator reveals challenges in Nepal's tunnel rescue efforts - WSLS

publisher.title: WSLS
full_article:
KATHMANDU – Filmmaker and drone pilot Manish Maharjan crossed into Nepal from China’s Tibet through Rasuwagadhi, a border crossing closest to where last week's catastrophic flooding began, two days before the disaster. Returning home, little did he know he would be using his professional skills to help with rescue efforts along a route he has known intimately from years of travel for work.

As authorities mobilized dozens of rescue and relief teams, Maharjan joined the Nepal Army’s rescue efforts a day after the flash floods, which have since killed more than 1,000 people and left thousands missing in Nepal and China.

Recommended Videos

Maharjan has been operating thermal drones to assist rescue teams, focused on locating and finding at least 900 workers who are still missing from 12 hydropower projects buried under mud and debris. About 500 of them are believed to be trapped inside power plant tunnels.

He said drones were effective in locating people who were stranded on hillsides and in isolated places, including caves.

“We used microphone speakers to call out to them. In some places, we even played songs and then waited for a response. That worked in a few cases and helped us locate people,” Maharjan said.

While drones have helped him rescue some stranded people in open areas, the tunnels present an entirely different challenge, he said.

“We found tunnels were filled with mud like toothpaste in a tube,” Maharjan said. “There was no hollow or empty space inside.”

The Aug. 26 flash floods started after a glacial collapse high in the Himalayan region. Scientists who studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

The rocks and melted water then swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water in Tibet and Nepal and causing widespread damage to critical infrastructure, including hydropower plants, roads, buildings and bridges in the region.

Some workers in the power plant tunnels managed to call for help when the disaster struck, and others who managed to flee reported their colleagues were still in the tunnels, according to Mohan Kumar Dangi, president of the Independent Power Producers’ Association. It was unclear whether rescuers have had any contact with the trapped workers since the initial calls for help.

As time slips away, rescuers are finding it increasingly difficult to locate these missing people. Experts say the first 72 hours are critical as the chances of survival drop without access to clean water. Access to breathable air is another key to survival.

Maharjan said the tunnel searches were challenging because of their difficult access and the absence of any empty space.

“I can only fly drones in tunnels that are long and straight,” he said. “Once there are bends, turns or zigzags, it becomes much harder to operate and search effectively.”

At the Rasuwagadhi hydropower project, Maharjan managed to send a drone to search deep inside and all the way to the end of the tunnel but found no sign of any life.

“We checked repeatedly but it was filled with mud and debris,” he said. “Looking at it, I could only imagine the force of the flood.”

___

Hussain reported from New Delhi.

(Daniel Ceng / Anadolu via Getty Images)

It’s still the rainy season in South Asia, and people in Nepal have come to expect increasingly extreme monsoon floods. But it wasn’t raining when the flood came this time. The water came not from the clouds but from the mountain itself.

The Himalayan glaciers, the planet’s Third Pole, are melting at an accelerating rate, along with the thawing permafrost that has long held this thin-air cryosphere together like glue.

On the morning of August 26, an enormous chunk of glacier and mountain at some 17,000 feet gave way on the north face of Langtang Lirung, setting off a cascade that sent a tsunami-like flood of water-and-rock slurry down the Bhotekoshi River on the Nepal-Tibet border and on down the heavily populated Trishuli River in the hills of central Nepal. As of this writing, more than 900 lives have been lost, with more than 4,200 missing, according to the Nepali government. (China’s state media reports “significant” losses, with more than 500 missing on the Tibet side of the border.)

Settlements, bridges, and roads along the river—including a vital trade route to China—have been swept away. And in addition to the cost in lives and property, more than 10 percent of Nepal’s crucial hydropower capacity has been destroyed.

How Nepal, a poor developing country of 30 million people that is among the most vulnerable to climate change, will pay for this disaster and many others—and whether it can adapt to climate change in meaningful ways—are not only economic questions but also deeply political and moral ones. (My forthcoming feature in The Nation ’s October issue looks at Nepal’s alarming climate crisis and its complex political and human rights situation.) To date, the world’s wealthiest and most historically responsible nations have failed to commit anywhere close to enough funding for adaptation and loss-and-damage in developing countries.

To understand the scale of this disaster’s impact on Nepal, and the prospect of international assistance, in the days after the flood I spoke with the Nepali climate expert Manjeet Dhakal, director of Climate Analytics South Asia in Kathmandu, who heads the United Nations’ Least Developed Countries Support Team. Dhakal has been closely involved in the creation of the UN’s climate loss-and-damage fund. He told me that though the fund is not yet fully operational, there are now internal discussions underway about providing emergency assistance to Nepal.

Current Issue September 2026 Issue

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

—Wen Stephenson



Wen Stephenson: The scale of this disaster is shocking, especially in terms of the human lives lost. The scope and scale of the damage is historic, yes?

Manjeet Dhakal: Yes, it’s historic. With climate change, the scientists have been warning about this. But the scale was something beyond the predictions.

WS: To put this disaster in context, what does it mean for Nepal that it struck this specific region? The Bhotekoshi-Trishuli river basin is both a crucial transport route to China and is also described as “the backbone of Nepal’s energy sector.” It’s reported that more than 10 percent of Nepal’s hydropower capacity was knocked out by this disaster. How important is hydropower for Nepal’s economy? And what does this mean going forward?

MD: There was about 500 megawatts of hydropower running, plus another roughly 200 megawatts that were in the last stages of construction, so roughly 700 to 750 megawatts has been heavily impacted.

And this is the peak season. Nepal has started exporting roughly 1,000 megawatts [1 gigawatt] of hydroelectricity to India during the rainy season, which has become a huge backbone for the economy.

So this obviously has set back the country in a number of ways, but the implication seems it will go much, much further. You mentioned the trade route. This is the new route that has been in operation for the past few years. There were 400-plus container trucks near Rasuwa, on the road with imports from China, with more than 1,000 drivers, workers and traders missing. The business will be heavily impacted, and in the longer run, with the energy infrastructure damage, the impact will go much higher.

Maybe this is a small thing, but there is also the electric vehicle exhibition going on in Kathmandu. [EV sales have surged in Nepal] and many of these new vehicles were there in the port of entry at the border and were completely washed away.

So you can imagine the trickle-down effect in the longer run. It’s massive.

WS: One thing to emphasize is that the pain of this disaster will reach Nepalis far beyond the immediate area where the flood has taken place. It will be felt from the Himalaya to the Tarai, in the plains. The last time we talked, two years ago, you mentioned how one major disaster can have a large impact on the country’s economy.

title: Nepal’s glacial collapse foreshadowed a future of climate disaster | Michael Mann - The Guardian
description: Nepal’s glacial collapse foreshadowed a future of climate disaster | Michael Mann  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
F or millennia, the high peaks of the Himalayas were held together by an invisible, frozen cement – permafrost and glacial ice that bound ancient rock into seemingly unshakable fortresses. But as the planet continues to warm, this alpine glue is liquefying.

The glacial collapse and deluge in Nepal and Tibet was not a freak weather event; it was the structural failure of a mountain itself, nature’s latest commentary on the deadly consequences of human-caused planetary warming. And it was the exclamation point on a summer of extremes, illustrating with a sole unnatural disaster the apocalyptic future that lies in store if we fail to take dramatic climate action.

As the death toll continues to mount – the latest count showed more than 900 dead and more than 4,400 individuals missing – this event has crystalized the climate crisis for many.

One reason is undoubtedly the sheer horror of what unfolded here. Chilling surveillance and eyewitness footage captured the horrific moment a 40mph wall of “liquid concrete” violently overtook fleeing crowds, instantly swallowing entire families and burying them beneath feet of thick, red-soaked silt. Another reason, however, is that the connection with climate change was unassailable in this case.

The Nepal floods seem a world away – but make no mistake, climate breakdown will affect us all | Nesrine Malik Read more

The torrent was the direct result of warming-induced glacial collapse, which dumped millions of tons of rock, unleashing a high-velocity wave of mud and debris. The new reality in the era of human-caused climate change, a CNN headline put it, is that “living downstream from a glacier has become a deadly liability”.

The impact of climate change on extreme weather, by contrast, is usually established though a statistical, rather than direct causal, connection. Through what is known as attribution science, climate scientists demonstrate the influence of climate change on the characteristics of an extreme weather event. It is analogous to how epidemiologists establish a linkage between cause (eg smoking cigarettes) and effect (lung cancer), through massive statistical evidence.

In the case of climate attribution, scientists run parallel climate model simulations, including a “control” simulation that represents a counterfactual world without human impact, and a “treatment” simulation where human drivers – primarily the increase in greenhouse gas concentrations – are included. They then compare how often a particular event happens in the two cases. If there is a substantial increase in occurrence of a particular event in the “treatment” simulation relative to the “control” simulation, then the extremeness of the event – and its human, societal or environmental impacts – can be “attributed” to climate change.

Critics might say that the connection here is merely statistical – almost circumstantial. But much as we are willing to attribute causality when a lifetime smoker contracts lung cancer because they were as much as 30 times more likely to do so because of their use of tobacco products, the extreme characteristics (unusually massive precipitation totals, high temperatures or destructive winds) of the weather event can be attributed to human-caused warming.

While the tragic and deadly Tibetan flood might have been the most prominent climate change-induced disaster this summer, it followed an unprecedented series of deadly, destructive and dangerous extreme weather events that can be connected to rising carbon pollution and the warming of our planet.

This summer of extremes began early. It started out with a March “heat dome” in the south-western US that yielded extremes of heat we only expect to see in mid-summer. The unprecedented extreme March heat was found by climate scientists to have been “virtually impossible” in the absence of human-caused warming.

Then came a midsummer-like May heat dome in the eastern US that smashed temperature records in my home city of Philadelphia. And within weeks, a European heat dome brought deadly triple-digit temperatures to large parts of France leading to the deaths of more than 3,000 people in Paris and nearly 6,000 for all of France. That was just the first of four record-breaking, back-to-back heatwaves in Europe that, by summer’s end, has cost the lives of more than 35,000 people. And yes, the deadly heat was attributed to climate change.

The record July heat combined with extreme dryness over large parts of western Europe – particularly France and Spain – to generate catastrophic wildfires that dominated the headlines for weeks, along with a viral photo of vacationers calmly lounging under a colorful umbrella while apocalyptic wildfire smoke billows in the background. The fires forced the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of people from their homes. And at the risk of sounding like a broken record: yes, it was formally attributed to human-caused warming.

Back in the US, we had our own wildfire problems. A combination of very hot and dry conditions over southern Ontario and the upper midwest led to huge wildfires generating plumes of smoke that choked the east coast for weeks. Air quality was rated hazardous in my home city of Philadelphia.

Nepal-Tibet flood: this is the cost of not acting in the face of the climate crisis | Sunil Acharya Read more

And yes, these wildfires – and indeed, the Canadian wildfires we now see summer after summer – can be attributed to climate change.

The summer of extreme weather disasters wasn’t done with us yet. In mid-August a historic “derecho” (a very wide, fast-moving line of severe thunderstorms associated typically with destructive, hurricane-strength straight-line destructive winds) struck the midwestern US with winds exceeding 100mph and devastating flooding, the better part of a million people from Illinois to Virginia were left without power.

While it is a challenge to apply attribution methods to these rare events, there is emerging evidence that climate change is making them more frequent and more damaging.

This past summer’s collective extreme weather disasters were an unmistakable consequence of the continued warming of our planet. The current administration’s policies – which were written by polluters themselves – are making things worse. Donald Trump and enabling congressional Republicans continue to double down on policies favoring fossil fuel extraction and dependence at the very time we need to be moving even more quickly away from fossil fuels toward clean energy.

These extreme events underscore the urgency of taking action now, and – while there are many things we can do – one of the greatest opportunities Americans will have to affect climate policy is the upcoming midterm election. You can make support for urgent and dramatic climate action a litmus test issue as you go to the voting booth.

जेना-जेना मरे वाला के संख्या बढ़ी रहलऽ छै – ताजा गिनती म॑ ९०० स॑ भी अधिक मौत आरू ४४०० स॑ भी अधिक व्यक्ति लापता होय गेलऽ छै – ई घटना न॑ बहुत लोगऽ लेली जलवायु संकट क॑ क्रिस्टलीकृत करी देल॑ छै ।

एकरऽ एक कारण निस्संदेह छै कि यहाँ जे कुछ खुललै ओकरऽ सरासर भयावहता । ठिठुरैत निगरानी आ प्रत्यक्षदर्शी फुटेज ओहि भयावह क्षण के कैद केलक जे 40 मील प्रति घंटा के “तरल कंक्रीट” के देबाल भागैत भीड़ के हिंसक रूप सं आगू बढ़ि गेल, तुरंत पूरा परिवार के निगल गेल आ ओकरा मोट, लाल रंग सं भीजल गाद के पैर के नीचा गाड़ि देलक. लेकिन एकरऽ एगो आरू कारण ई छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ जुड़ाव ई मामला म॑ अप्रत्याशित छेलै ।

नेपालक बाढ़ि एक दुनियाँ दूर बुझाइत अछि – मुदा गलती नहि करू, जलवायु टूटला सँ हम सब प्रभावित होयत | नेसरीन मलिक और पढ़ें

ई धार गर्म होय के कारण हिमनदी केरऽ पतन के सीधा परिणाम छेलै, जेकरा स॑ लाखों टन चट्टान फेंकलऽ गेलै, जेकरा स॑ थाल आरू मलबा केरऽ उच्च वेग वाला लहर निकललै । सीएनएन केरऽ एगो हेडलाइन न॑ कहलकै कि मानव-जनित जलवायु परिवर्तन के दौर म॑ नया वास्तविकता ई छै कि “ग्लेशियर स॑ नीचें रहना एगो घातक दायित्व बनी गेलऽ छै” ।

एकरऽ विपरीत चरम मौसम प॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ प्रभाव आमतौर प॑ प्रत्यक्ष कारण के बजाय सांख्यिकीय संबंध के बावजूद स्थापित होय छै । जेकरा एट्रिब्यूशन साइंस के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय छै, ओकरऽ माध्यम स॑ जलवायु वैज्ञानिक एगो चरम मौसमी घटना के विशेषता प॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन के प्रभाव के प्रदर्शन करै छै । ई एकरऽ अनुरूप छै कि कोना महामारी विज्ञानी कारण (जैना सिगरेट पीना) आरू प्रभाव (फेफड़ा के कैंसर) के बीच संबंध स्थापित करै छै, विशाल सांख्यिकीय साक्ष्य के माध्यम स॑ ।

जलवायु विशेषता के मामला म॑ वैज्ञानिक समानांतर जलवायु मॉडल सिमुलेशन चलाबै छै, जेकरा म॑ एगो “नियंत्रण” सिमुलेशन शामिल छै जे मानव प्रभाव के बिना एक प्रतितथ्यात्मक दुनिया के प्रतिनिधित्व करै छै, आरू एक “उपचार” सिमुलेशन जहाँ मानव चालक – मुख्य रूप स॑ ग्रीनहाउस गैस के सांद्रता म॑ वृद्धि – क॑ शामिल करलऽ जाय छै । तखन ओ सभ तुलना करैत छथि जे दुनू मामला मे कोनो विशेष घटना कतेक बेर होइत अछि । यदि “नियंत्रण” अनुकरण कें सापेक्ष “उपचार” अनुकरण मे कोनों विशेष घटना कें घटित होय मे काफी वृद्धि होयत छै, तखन घटना कें चरमता – आ ओकर मानवीय, सामाजिक या पर्यावरणीय प्रभावक – कें जलवायु परिवर्तन कें “श्रेणी” देल जा सकय छै.

आलोचक लोकनि कहि सकैत छथि जे एहि ठामक संबंध मात्र सांख्यिकीय अछि – लगभग परिस्थितिजन्य अछि । लेकिन जेतना हम्मं॑ कारणता के कारण बताबै लेली तैयार छियै जब॑ जीवन भर धूम्रपान करै वाला क॑ फेफड़ा के कैंसर होय जाय छै, कैन्हेंकि ओकरा तंबाकू उत्पादऽ के इस्तेमाल के कारण ३० गुना स॑ भी अधिक संभावना छेलै, मौसम केरऽ घटना केरऽ चरम विशेषता (असामान्य रूप स॑ भारी वर्षा केरऽ कुल, उच्च तापमान या विनाशकारी हवा) क॑ मानव कारण स॑ गरम होय के कारण मानलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै ।

जहाँ ई दुखद आरू घातक तिब्बती बाढ़ ई गर्मी म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ पैदा होय वाला सबस॑ प्रमुख आपदा होय सकै छै, वहीं ई घातक, विनाशकारी आरू खतरनाक चरम मौसमी घटना के अभूतपूर्व श्रृंखला के बाद आबी गेलऽ छै जेकरा बढ़तऽ कार्बन प्रदूषण आरू हमरऽ ग्रह केरऽ गर्मी स॑ जोड़लऽ जाब॑ सकै छै ।

चरम सीमाक ई गर्मी जल्दी शुरू भ गेल। एकरऽ शुरुआत दक्षिण-पश्चिमी अमेरिका म॑ मार्च केरऽ “हीट डोम” स॑ भेलऽ छेलै जेकरा स॑ गर्मी केरऽ चरम पैदावार होय छेलै जेकरा स॑ हम्में केवल गर्मी के मध्य म॑ ही देखै के उम्मीद करै छियै । मार्च केरऽ अभूतपूर्व चरम गर्मी क॑ जलवायु वैज्ञानिकऽ न॑ मानव के कारण गर्मी के अभाव म॑ “प्रायः असंभव” पाबै छेलै ।

तखन पूर्वी अमेरिकामें मध्य गर्मी सन मई गर्मीक गुंबद आयल जे हमर गृहनगर फिलाडेल्फियामें तापमानक रिकॉर्ड तोड़ि देलक. आरू हफ्ता भर के भीतर यूरोपीय हीट डोम न॑ फ्रांस केरऽ बड़ऽ हिस्सा म॑ घातक तीन अंकऽ के तापमान लानल॑ छेलै जेकरा स॑ पेरिस म॑ ३,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलै आरू पूरा फ्रांस म॑ लगभग ६,००० लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलै । ई यूरोप केरऽ चारो रिकॉर्ड तोड़ऽ वाला, बैक-टू-बैक गर्मी केरऽ लहरऽ म॑ स॑ पहलऽ ही छेलै जेकरा म॑ गर्मी केरऽ अंत तलक ३५,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के जान गेलऽ छै । आ हाँ, घातक गर्मी के कारण जलवायु परिवर्तन मानल गेल।

जुलाई केरऽ रिकॉर्ड गर्मी न॑ पश्चिमी यूरोप केरऽ बड़ऽ हिस्सा – खास करी क॑ फ्रांस आरू स्पेन – प॑ अत्यधिक शुष्कता के साथ मिल क॑ विनाशकारी जंगली आग पैदा करी देलकै जे हफ्ता भर स॑ सुर्खी म॑ हावी रहलै, साथ ही साथ छुट्टी मनाबै वाला लोगऽ के एगो वायरल फोटो भी छेलै जे शांति स॑ रंगीन छतरी के नीचें आराम करी रहलऽ छै जबकि पृष्ठभूमि म॑ एपोकैलिप्टिक जंगली आग के धुँआ लहरै छै । आगि के कारण लाखों लोक के घर सं बाहर निकालय पड़ल. आ टूटल रिकार्ड जकाँ आवाज देबाक जोखिम पर : हँ, एकरा औपचारिक रूपें मनुक्खक कारण वार्मिंगक कारण मानल गेल छल.

अमेरिका में वापसी में हमरा सब के अपन जंगली आगि के समस्या छल. दक्षिणी ओन्टारियो आरू ऊपरी मध्य पश्चिम के ऊपर बहुत गर्मी आरू शुष्क परिस्थिति के संयोजन के कारण विशाल जंगली आग लगलै जेकरा स॑ धुँआ के धुँआ पैदा होय गेलै जे पूर्वी तट क॑ हफ्ता भर तलक गला घोंटलकै । हमर गृहनगर फिलाडेल्फिया में हवाक गुणवत्ता खतरनाक मानल गेल छल.

नेपाल-तिब्बत बाढ़ : जलवायु संकट के सामना नै करला के लागत छै | सुनील आचार्य Read more

आ हाँ, एहि जंगली आगि – आ सचमुच, कनाडाक जंगली आगि जे आब गर्मीक बाद गर्मी देखैत छी – जलवायु परिवर्तनक कारण भ सकैत अछि.

मौसमक चरम आपदा’क गर्मी हमरा सभक संग एखन धरि नहि भ’ सकल छल. अगस्त केरऽ मध्य म॑ एगो ऐतिहासिक “डेरेचो” (एक बहुत चौड़ा, तेज गति स॑ चलै वाला गंभीर गरजऽ के लाइन जे आम तौर प॑ विनाशकारी, तूफान-शक्ति वाला सीधी-रेखा विनाशकारी हवा स॑ जुड़लऽ छै) न॑ मध्य पश्चिमी अमेरिका म॑ 100 मील प्रति घंटा स॑ अधिक हवा आरू विनाशकारी बाढ़ के साथ आबी गेलै, इलिनोइस स॑ ल॑ क॑ वर्जीनिया तलक के लाख लोगऽ के बेहतर हिस्सा बिजली स॑ रहित रह॑ गेलै ।

जहाँ ई दुर्लभ घटना सब पर एट्रिब्यूशन विधि लागू करना एगो चुनौती छै, वहीं ई बात के सबूत सामने आबी रहलऽ छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन एकरा अधिक बार आरू अधिक नुकसानदेह बनाबै छै ।

ई बीतलऽ गर्मी म॑ सामूहिक चरम मौसमी आपदा हमरऽ ग्रह केरऽ लगातार गर्मी केरऽ अचूक परिणाम छेलै । वर्तमान प्रशासन के नीति – जे प्रदूषक स्वयं लिखने छलाह – हालात आओर खराब क’ रहल अछि. डोनाल्ड ट्रंप आरू सक्षम बनाबै वाला कांग्रेसी रिपब्लिकन जीवाश्म ईंधन निष्कर्षण आरू निर्भरता के पक्ष म॑ नीति प॑ दोगुना काम जारी रखै छै, ठीक वू समय म॑ जब॑ हमरा जीवाश्म ईंधन स॑ दूर आरू तेजी स॑ स्वच्छ ऊर्जा के तरफ बढ़ै के जरूरत छै ।

ई चरम घटना सब अब॑ कार्रवाई करै के तात्कालिकता क॑ रेखांकित करै छै, आरू – जब॑ कि बहुत सारा काम हम्मं॑ करी सकै छियै – जलवायु नीति क॑ प्रभावित करै लेली अमेरिकी लोगऽ क॑ एक सबसें बड़ऽ अवसर आबै वाला मध्यावधि चुनाव छै । मतदान बूथ पर जाइत काल अहां तत्काल आओर नाटकीय जलवायु कार्रवाई के समर्थन के लिटमस टेस्ट के मुद्दा बना सकय छी.

KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescue teams with search dogs combed through mud, rocks and debris Tuesday in Nepal and China looking for thousands of people still missing after catastrophic flooding tore through communities across the Himalayas , leaving more than 1,000 dead.

Nepal’s disaster agency said Tuesday that 987 deaths had been counted there, with 3,916 people missing, including 583 foreigners. Chinese authorities, in their latest update on Sunday, reported 16 deaths and 546 people still missing, including 261 foreigners.

The scale of last week’s disaster was hampering rescue efforts in both regions, with landslides, destroyed roads and widespread damage cutting off remote areas. Crews faced challenging conditions as they searched unstable terrain and piles of debris, raising fears the death toll could rise as rescuers reach isolated communities.

At least 168 people were killed and more than 1,300 were missing after catastrophic and deadly torrents of floods and mud swept through several communities along the Nepal-China following a glacier collapse.

In Nepal, rescuers were racing to reach hundreds of workers believed to be trapped inside tunnels at hydropower projects damaged by the floods. About 900 workers are missing from 12 projects, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to Nepalese authorities.

Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal’s army spokesperson, said teams assisted by foreign experts were working at several hydropower projects. Visuals released by the army showed rescue teams entering dark, debris-filled tunnels, wading through mud and water and climbing over rocks as they searched for signs of life.

On the Chinese side, rescue crews scoured areas hit by mudslides, particularly around the Gyirong Port border crossing, which was destroyed.

Some rescuers, aided by search dogs, searched gaps among rocks and debris for signs of life. Other teams used heavy machinery to clear a major highway leading to Gyirong Port, hoping to clear the way for equipment, personnel and supplies to reach the disaster zone, according to China’s state-run Global Times newspaper.

The disaster began with a glacial collapse high in the Himalayas

The Aug. 26 disaster began with a chain of events high in the Himalayas . A glacial collapse sent large amounts of rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream.

Scientists studying satellite imagery said the collapse appears to have involved the failure of bedrock beneath a glacier in the Himalayan region. The rockfall was powerful enough to register as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

The resulting surge of water and debris entered rivers that flow through valleys in Tibet and Nepal, causing them to rise rapidly. Floodwaters swept away homes, buildings, roads and bridges and carried mud and rocks downstream.

Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah said that the disaster highlighted the need for action to combat climate change.

“This incident has indicated that the risks we face in the Himalayan region are increasing with climate change,” Shah said in a social media post Monday night. “Therefore, this region must be alert, and at the same time, it is time for us to strongly raise the issue of disasters caused by climate change before the international community.”

नेपाल केरऽ आपदा एजेंसी मंगलवार क॑ कहलकै कि वहाँ ९८७ लोगऽ के मौत के गिनती करलऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ ५८३ विदेशी सहित ३,९१६ लोग लापता छै । चीनी अधिकारी रविदिन अपन ताजा अपडेट मे 16 लोकक मौत आ 546 लोक एखनो लापता अछि, जाहि मे 261 विदेशी सेहो शामिल छथि।

title: Relief as Australian missing in Nepal-Tibet flood disaster found alive - The Guardian
description: Relief as Australian missing in Nepal-Tibet flood disaster found alive  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
A second Australian believed to be missing after floods ravaged the Nepal-Tibet border last week has been found alive.

The person made contact with officials from the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Dfat) on Tuesday from Tibet.

They are receiving support from Australian consular officers and have spoken with their family.

How the deadly Nepal and Tibet flash flood unfolded – a visual guide Read more

Another Australian, 25-year-old Cara Severino, was safely located last week. The total number still missing is 42.

The foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, said the government was “incredibly thankful” the person had been found.

“It’s hard to imagine the sense of relief their loved ones must be feeling after what will have been an incredibly harrowing few days.”

Due to privacy obligations the foreign affairs department was unable to provide further details about the individual.

A map of the flood affected area

The death toll from the ⁠unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud ​and debris on Wednesday last week has risen to 939 people, with 16 more dead reported in Tibet.

More than 4,400 are missing.

Wong said the government needed to “remain realistic” about the days ahead.

“Communications remain difficult, infrastructure has been destroyed and many areas are still difficult to reach,” she said.

Nepal rescuers race to reach hundreds feared trapped in hydropower tunnels Read more

“As each day passes, our grave concerns for those still unaccounted for inevitably grow.”

“Our thoughts remain firmly with all those waiting for news of family and friends, and with the search and rescue teams working in extraordinarily difficult circumstances.”

Australia has sent a $8m assistance package for affected communities on the border between Nepal and the Chinese region of Tibet.

Nepal has deployed nearly 20,000 security personnel to support search and rescue, and Chinese state media has reported that 2,141 emergency personnel have been deployed.

title: Nepal-Tibet flood deaths pass 1,000 as police ask relatives for DNA to identify victims - The Guardian
description: Nepal-Tibet flood deaths pass 1,000 as police ask relatives for DNA to identify victims  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
Nepali rescuers have built temporary bridges to reach remote areas and dug through the ruins of hydropower projects in the Himalayas to rescue hundreds of trapped workers, as the death toll passed 1,000 nearly ⁠a week after devastating ​floods left a trail of destruction across the country’s towns and valleys.

About 600 people remain stuck in several devastated hydropower stations that have become the focus of rescue efforts. The prime ⁠minister, Balendra Shah, said more than 11,000 people had been rescued across the affected region, and power and communication lines had been restored in some areas.

“Thousands of citizens have lost their homes, families, loved ones and property,” Shah said.

Headteacher saves 900 children from deadly flash flood in Nepal Read more

Six days after the catastrophe struck the Himalayan border region, 4,400 people were still missing in Nepal and Tibet. Police in Kathmandu have urged relatives of missing tourists to provide DNA samples to assist identification efforts.

In a statement posted to social media, Nepal police on Monday asked relatives of those missing to “provide a fresh blood sample for DNA profiling and two passport-sized photographs” to the pathology laboratory at the Nepal police hospital in Kathmandu, or the nearest district police office.

Among Nepal’s list of the missing are 592 foreigners, including tourists who had come for mountain trekking and Hindu pilgrims seeking spiritual peace at Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash, from countries such as India, the US, UK, Australia and Canada.

Relatives abroad have been requested to undergo DNA profiling at an authorised laboratory and to “send a soft copy of the DNA profile to Nepal police’s official email address”.

In some of Nepal’s flood-affected areas, hundreds of unidentified bodies have already been buried because they are decomposing and there is no room left in hospitals or morgues.

People search posters of those missing in Nepal flood

At the police hospital in Kathmandu on Tuesday, more than 100 people were waiting to have their blood sampled.

Among them was Prakaiti Jurnj. Her mother was still missing, but the family had been able to identify her father’s body from a photograph on the wall outside the teaching hospital, where images of the deceased have been posted in an effort to identify the victims.

“Both my father and mother, they were in the village in Nukawot. They were both swept away by the flood,” she said. “We haven’t heard from them since Wednesday. We found my father’s body; my brother saw the photo on the wall.”

She was waiting for her two other siblings, who live in the UK, to arrive on Tuesday so they could all try to get up to the village. She said she wanted to contact her grandmother or sister-in-law, who she thinks both survived the flood because their house is further up the mountain. Their village was still in a blackout, and making contact was impossible.

“I can’t go there; the situation is very bad,” she said. “I can’t go up there alone. I am not sure if we’ll be able to get them.”

The disaster was triggered by a glacier collapse that sent a deluge of ice, rock and mud through Nepal’s border region with China, posing a massive challenge for the country’s six-month-old government.

The region is vulnerable to flooding and landslides, and extreme weather events such as intense monsoons and melting glaciers have become more common because of warming due to human-caused climate change.

In a late-night social media post, Shah said aid worth more than $42m had poured into the country, but that Nepalis were reeling. “The government understands the ​immense pain they are enduring. The path ahead is to ‌support them through this suffering and help ‌them return to normal life through rehabilitation,” the prime minister said.

Shah also said that 279 workers had so far been rescued from hydropower projects, where authorities estimated close to 1,000 people had been trapped. Days after the disaster, hope was rapidly diminisging that any of those trapped in a series of tunnels could be alive.

1:02 Nepal rescue teams work to reach over 900 people believed trapped in hydropower tunnels - video

Pictures and videos shared by rescue teams showed earth-moving equipment digging and shovelling mud and rocks under lights in the dark of the night. Soldiers used torchlight in a big pit they had created to look for space to get into one tunnel.

Chinese state media coverage has focused largely on the official response, highlighting the deployment of firefighters, the People’s Liberation Army and instructions from top leaders. Little is known about victims on the Chinese side.

The flood was “caused by glacier instability under the long-term effects of global warming”, China’s state broadcaster said on Monday.

Shah said the ​catastrophic event signalled the growing risks that the Himalayan region faces. “The region must therefore remain vigilant. The time has come for us to strongly raise before the international community the disasters we are experiencing as a consequence of climate change,” he wrote in his post.

शाह कहलनि जे, हजारों नागरिक के घर, परिवार, प्रियजन आ संपत्ति के नुकसान भेल अछि।

नेपालमे घातक झटका बाढिसँ ९०० बच्चाकेँ बँचौलन्हि हेडटीचर Read more

हिमालय सीमा क्षेत्रमे प्रलय भेलाक ६ दिन बाद सेहो नेपाल आ तिब्बतमे ४४०० गोटे लापता अछि । काठमांडूके प्रहरी लापता पर्यटकके परिजनसँ पहिचानके प्रयासमे सहयोगके लेल डीएनए नमुना उपलब्ध कराबऽ आग्रह केने अछि ।

सोशल मीडिया पर देल गेल बयान मे नेपाल पुलिस सोमदिन लापता लोकनिक परिजन सँ काठमांडू स्थित नेपाल पुलिस अस्पतालक पैथोलॉजी प्रयोगशाला, वा नजदीकी जिला पुलिस कार्यालय मे “डीएनए प्रोफाइलिंग लेल ताजा खूनक नमूना आ दू टा पासपोर्ट आकारक फोटो उपलब्ध कराबय” लेल कहलक अछि।

नेपाल केरऽ लापता लोगऽ के सूची म॑ ५९२ विदेशी शामिल छै, जेकरा म॑ भारत, अमेरिका, ब्रिटेन, ऑस्ट्रेलिया आरू कनाडा जैसनऽ देशऽ स॑ माउंटेन ट्रेकिंग लेली ऐलऽ पर्यटक आरू तिब्बत केरऽ पवित्र कैलाश पर्वत प॑ आध्यात्मिक शांति चाहै वाला हिन्दू तीर्थयात्री भी शामिल छै ।

विदेश मे रिश्तेदार स आग्रह कैल गेल अछि जे ओ अधिकृत प्रयोगशाला मे डीएनए प्रोफाइलिंग करथि आ “डीएनए प्रोफाइल क सॉफ्ट कॉपी नेपाल पुलिस क आधिकारिक ईमेल पता पर पठाउ”।

नेपालक किछु बाढ़ि प्रभावित क्षेत्र मे सैकड़ों अज्ञात लाश सड़ि रहल अछि आ अस्पताल वा मुर्दाघर मे कोनो जगह नहि रहबाक कारणेँ पहिने सँ दफनाओल गेल अछि ।

नेपाल बाढ़ि मे लापता लोकक पोस्टर मे लोक खोजि रहल अछि

ओहि मे प्रकैती जुरंज सेहो छल। हुनकऽ मां अभी भी लापता छेली, लेकिन परिवार टीचिंग अस्पताल के बाहर देवाल प॑ बनलऽ फोटो स॑ हुनकऽ पिता केरऽ शव के पहचान करी सकलऽ छेलै, जहां पीड़ितऽ के पहचान करै के कोशिश म॑ मृतकऽ के तस्वीर लगाय देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

ओ कहलीह जे हमर पिता आ मां दुनू गोटे नुकावोट मे गाम मे छलाह, दुनू गोटे बाढ़ि मे बह गेलाह। “बुध दिन सँ हुनका सभक कोनो खबरि नहि भेटल अछि. हमरा सभ केँ हमर पिताजी’क लाश भेटल;हमर भाइ केँ देबाल पर फोटो देखलक.”

ओ बजलीह, “हम ओत’ नहि जा सकैत छी, स्थिति बहुत खराब अछि.” “हम असगरे ओत’ ऊपर नहि जा सकैत छी, हमरा यकीन नहि अछि जे हम सभ ओकरा सभ केँ पाबि सकब कि नहि.”

ई आपदा ग्लेशियर केरऽ गिरला स॑ शुरू होय गेलऽ छेलै जेकरा स॑ चीन के साथ नेपाल केरऽ सीमावर्ती क्षेत्र म॑ बर्फ, चट्टान आरू कीचड़ के बाढ़ आबी गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा स॑ देश केरऽ छह महीना पुरानऽ सरकार लेली एगो बड़ऽ चुनौती छेलै ।

ई क्षेत्र बाढ़ आरू भूस्खलन के शिकार छै, आरू मानव के कारण जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण गर्मी के कारण तीव्र मानसून आरू पिघलना ग्लेशियर जैसनऽ चरम मौसमी घटना अधिक आम होय गेलऽ छै ।

देर राति सोशल मीडिया पर देल गेल पोस्ट मे शाह कहलनि जे, देश मे 42 मिलियन डॉलर सं बेसी के सहायता के बरसात भेल अछि, मुदा नेपाली डगमगा रहल अछि. प्रधानमंत्री कहलनि जे, सरकार हुनका सब के जे अपार पीड़ा झेल रहल अछि ओकरा बुझैत अछि, आगू के रास्ता अछि जे एहि दुख के माध्यम सं हुनका सब के सहयोग करी आ पुनर्वास के माध्यम सं हुनका सब के सामान्य जीवन में वापसी में मदद करी।

शाह इहो कहलनि जे, एखन धरि जलविद्युत परियोजना सं 279 मजदूर के बचाओल गेल अछि, जतय अधिकारि के अनुमान अछि जे करीब एक हजार लोक फंसल अछि. आपदा के कुछ दिन बाद आशा तेजी सें कम होय रहलऽ छेलै कि सुरंगऽ के श्रृंखला में फंसलऽ कोय भी जीवित होय सकै छै ।

1:02 नेपाल बचाव दल जलविद्युत सुरंग मे फंसल मानल गेल 900 स बेसी लोक तक पहुंचेबा लेल काज करैत अछि - वीडियो

बचाव दल द्वारा साझा कएल गेल तस्वीर आ वीडियो मे राति के अन्हार मे धरती के हिलाबय वाला उपकरण के रोशनी के नीचा कीचड़ आ चट्टान के खोदैत आ फावड़ा सं फेकैत देखाओल गेल अछि. सैनिक सब अपन बनाओल एकटा पैघ गड्ढा में मशाल के रोशनी के उपयोग क एकटा सुरंग में घुसय लेल जगह खोजैत छल.

चीन केरऽ सरकारी मीडिया कवरेज म॑ काफी हद तलक आधिकारिक प्रतिक्रिया प॑ ध्यान देलऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ दमकलकर्मी, पीपुल्स लिबरेशन आर्मी केरऽ तैनाती आरू शीर्ष नेता सिनी के निर्देश प॑ प्रकाश डाललऽ गेलऽ छै । चीनी पक्ष के पीड़ित के बारे मे बहुत कम जानकारी अछि.

चीन केरऽ सरकारी प्रसारक न॑ सोमवार क॑ कहलकै कि ई बाढ़ “ग्लोशियर वार्मिंग केरऽ दीर्घकालिक प्रभाव के तहत ग्लेशियर अस्थिरता के वजह स॑ पैदा होय गेलऽ छै ।

शाह नँ कहलकै कि ई विनाशकारी घटना हिमालयी क्षेत्र मँ बढ़तौ जोखिम के संकेत दै छै । ओ अपन पोस्ट मे लिखलनि जे, एहि लेल एहि क्षेत्र कए सतर्क रहबाक चाही, समय आबि गेल अछि जे जलवायु परिवर्तन क परिणामस्वरूप हमरा सब कए जे आपदा भ रहल अछि ओकरा अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय क सामने मजबूती स उठाबी।

More than 1,000 people have been confirmed dead following catastrophic flash flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border last week, with nearly 4,000 others still unaccounted for.

The Nepal National Disaster Management Authority reported 1,003 recovered bodies as of Tuesday afternoon, September 1.

Nepal's disaster agency put the nationwide missing count at 3,916 people, according to a 1 p.m. Tuesday update.

On the Chinese side of the border, authorities separately reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing, with 261 of those missing being foreign nationals, according to ABC News.

What Triggered the Flooding

The disaster began around 8:40 a.m. on Wednesday, August 27, when a wall of ice, water and debris descended from mountains along the Nepal-Tibet frontier.

ABC News reported that an analysis of verified video and satellite imagery showed destruction extending at least 62 miles downriver into Nepal along the Trishuli River, burying buildings and damaging bridges and road links throughout the region.

Tunnels Become Focus of Search Efforts

Rescuers are concentrating part of their search on tunnels at hydropower projects in the Rasuwa district.

About 900 workers are unaccounted for at those sites, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped underground, according to reporting by News10NBC.

The Nepali Army said 279 people were pulled out alive from hydropower areas during the initial response phase.

More than 9,200 army troops are deployed across Rasuwa, Dhading, Nawalparasi East, and Chitwan, where they are conducting search operations, clearing blocked roads and providing emergency medical care.

Helicopter and fixed-wing aircraft are being used to reach communities cut off by destroyed infrastructure. At least 11,814 people have been rescued so far.

Tourists Among the Missing

Nepal's tourism board listed at least 747 people missing in Rasuwa district alone, including approximately 583 foreign tourists.

At least 64 of those tourists are from the United States, based on lists published by the board.

On the Chinese side, rescuers are working around areas hit by mudslides near the Gyirong Port border crossing, which was destroyed in the disaster.

Relief Collections Underway

Community organizations in the United States have begun collecting aid. The Bhutanese Community of Greater Rochester, New York, is gathering food and essential supplies at three locations in the city.

The group described the flooding as a devastating moment for Nepali-speaking communities and called for solidarity with those affected.

Elevate Nepal, an Arizona-based nonprofit, is also fundraising for disaster relief.

The group said one of the hardest-hit communities, Trishuli Bazaar, is near a school it constructed in 2018, and that it is working with local partners to direct its response.

नेपालके आपदा एजेन्सीके अनुसार राष्ट्रव्यापी लापताके संख्या ३,९१६ जनौने अछि । मंगल दिन अपडेट।

27 अगस्त बुधदिन भोर करीब 8:40 बजे नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा पर पहाड़ स बर्फ, पानि आ मलबा क देबाल उतरि गेल।

एबीसी न्यूज के रिपोर्ट के अनुसार सत्यापित वीडियो आरू उपग्रह इमेजरी के विश्लेषण में त्रिशुली नदी के साथ नेपाल में कम से कम 62 मील नीचें तक फैललऽ विनाश केरऽ घटना सामने ऐलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ भवन गाड़लऽ गेलऽ छै आरू पूरा क्षेत्र म॑ पुल आरू सड़क संपर्क क॑ नुकसान पहुँचैलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

सुरंग खोज प्रयास के केंद्र बनैत अछि

लापता के बीच पर्यटक

नेपालक पर्यटन बोर्ड मात्र रसुवा जिला मे कम सँ कम ७४७ लोकक सूची देलक जाहि मे लगभग ५८३ विदेशी पर्यटक सेहो शामिल अछि ।

title: Smell of death hangs over rescue efforts in Nepal as deaths pass 1,000 - NBC News
description: Smell of death hangs over rescue efforts in Nepal as deaths pass 1,000  NBC News
publisher.title: NBC News
full_article:
BIDUR, Nepal — The overwhelming stench of death is crushing hopes that more survivors will be found in this Nepalese town devastated by last week’s catastrophic floods.

Workers in white hazmat suits unload bodies from a stream of ambulances in Bidur, a town in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on Tuesday. They place the wrapped bodies onto blue tarp in a cordoned off area.

Helicopters, both military and civilian aircraft that in better days would be used for commercial tours, take off packed with aid before returning with survivors in need of medical care.

Kalpana Shrestha, a nurse who works in capital Kathmandu, is desperate. Ten members of her family are missing — her two sisters and their children — are missing.

Kalpana Shrestha. Adam Galica / NBC News

“I have shared their photos with journalists, on social media and YouTube but I have not got any response at all,” she said speaking with NBC News in Kathmandu. She added that her loved ones disappeared in Betrawati, a town some 60 miles from the capital that was obliterated in the flooding.

“I have posted so much that my fingers started shaking and trembling,” said Shrestha, 35. “My mind has stopped working. But even so, we have not stopped posting.”

More than 1,000 have been declared dead in Nepal after last week’s devastating floods, according to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Over 3,915 others are still missing, including at least 583 foreign nationals. In Tibet, at least 16 people were killed and 546 are missing, according to CGTN, China’s English-language satellite news channel.

At least 80 Americans are among the missing in Nepal.

More than 10,000 people have been rescued so far, including 252 foreign nationals, the United Nations says.

The disaster, which was triggered by a glacier collapse and landslide on Nepal’s border with China, is now considered Nepal’s deadliest natural disaster since the April 2015 earthquake that killed around 9,000 people in Nepal.

A poster featuring Kalpona Shrestha’s missing family members. Adam Galica / NBC News

Shrestha said she felt that the government was “not doing enough work to search and rescue to locate” her family. She also noted that access to her village was still difficult after the floods.

“Our brothers did try but failed to reach them and had to return home,” she said. “The road is gone, there is no access at all.”

Access remains the single biggest obstacle to response efforts, with roads passable only as far as Nuwakot and some sections of highway linking Kathmandu to the hardest areas still completely blocked, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs.

And the bodies that have been recovered pose a huge challenge to authorities, who are using at least 21 hospitals in a string of districts to store remains, according to Nepal’s disaster agency. In some cases, bodies are being buried to prevent any risk of infection, with hopes they will be later identified so the remains can be returned to loved ones.

A health worker sprays disinfectant following flash floods in Devighat on Monday. Arun Sankar / AFP via Getty Images

Speaking with NBC News in Pokhara, Nabin Karki, a superintendent of police, said authorities were collecting DNA samples and display photos of the bodies found so in hopes that family members might be able to identify them.

Relatives of those missing can provide blood samples for DNA testing, he said, and if a match is found the body can be taken from the burial site and handed over to the family for a funeral.

Updated: 7:01 AM EDT Sep 1, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ By SHRISTI KAFLE and SHEIKH SAALIQ, Associated Press

Rescue teams with search dogs combed through mud, rocks and debris Tuesday in Nepal and China, looking for thousands of people still missing after catastrophic flooding tore through communities across the Himalayas, leaving more than 1,000 dead.

Nepal's disaster agency said Tuesday that 987 deaths had been counted there, with 3,916 people missing, including 583 foreigners. Chinese authorities, in their latest update on Sunday, reported 16 deaths and 546 people still missing, including 261 foreigners.

The scale of last week's disaster was hampering rescue efforts in both regions, with landslides, destroyed roads and widespread damage cutting off remote areas. Crews faced challenging conditions as they searched unstable terrain and piles of debris, raising fears the death toll could rise as rescuers reach isolated communities.

Rescuers race to reach missing hydropower workers

In Nepal, rescuers were racing to reach hundreds of workers believed to be trapped inside tunnels at hydropower projects damaged by the floods. About 900 workers are missing from 12 projects, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to Nepalese authorities.

Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal's army spokesperson, said teams assisted by foreign experts were working at several hydropower projects. Visuals released by the army showed rescue teams entering dark, debris-filled tunnels, wading through mud and water and climbing over rocks as they searched for signs of life.

On the Chinese side, rescue crews scoured areas hit by mudslides, particularly around the Gyirong Port border crossing, which was destroyed.

Some rescuers, aided by search dogs, searched gaps among rocks and debris for signs of life. Other teams used heavy machinery to clear a major highway leading to Gyirong Port, hoping to clear the way for equipment, personnel and supplies to reach the disaster zone, according to China's state-run Global Times newspaper.

Relief operations expand to reach stranded communities

At least 11,814 people have been rescued so far, according to Nepalese authorities. Emergency crews were using helicopters and other aircraft to reach stranded communities in areas where roads and bridges have been destroyed by the flooding and landslides.

Authorities on Tuesday also stepped up efforts to provide assistance to survivors in areas where roads and other transportation routes had been damaged or cut off.

Satellite images show bedrock and glacier collapsed on Nepal-China border, then rivers flooded

Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said China's second batch of relief supplies for Nepal was expected to ship Tuesday, including drones, DNA testing and water purification equipment. Chinese DNA testing experts will also help Nepal identify bodies, he said.

Bimal Sharma, a helicopter pilot who has been flying rescue and relief missions since the disaster began, said he was shocked to see the devastation in Timure, a border town close to Tibet that he has known for years.

"It felt like I was flying over an entirely different landscape," he said.

Sharma said he has had little opportunity to speak with the people he rescued, but their expressions told him how deeply the disaster had affected them.

"I can see the pain in their eyes. It's heartbreaking," he said.

The disaster began with a glacial collapse high in the Himalayas

The Aug. 26 disaster began with a chain of events high in the Himalayas. A glacial collapse sent large amounts of rock, ice and meltwater into valleys below, triggering powerful floods downstream.

Scientists studying satellite imagery said the collapse appears to have involved the failure of bedrock beneath a glacier in the Himalayan region. The rockfall was powerful enough to register as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event.

The resulting surge of water and debris entered rivers that flow through valleys in Tibet and Nepal, causing them to rise rapidly. Floodwaters swept away homes, buildings, roads and bridges and carried mud and rocks downstream.

Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah said that the disaster highlighted the need for action to combat climate change.

"This incident has indicated that the risks we face in the Himalayan region are increasing with climate change," Shah said in a social media post Monday night. "Therefore, this region must be alert, and at the same time, it is time for us to strongly raise the issue of disasters caused by climate change before the international community."

___

Saaliq reported from New Delhi. Associated Press journalists E. Eduardo Castillo in Beijing, Kanis Leung in Hong Kong and Aijaz Hussain in New Delhi contributed to this report.

लापता जलविद्युत मजदूर तक पहुंचबाक लेल बचावकर्मी दौड़ैत अछि

नेपालमे बाढ़िसँ क्षतिग्रस्त जलविद्युत परियोजनामे सुरंगक भीतर फँसल सैकड़ों मजदूर लग पहुँचबाक लेल बचावकर्मी दौड़ल छल । नेपाली अधिकारी के अनुसार १२ परियोजना स करीब ९०० मजदूर लापता अछि, जाहि मे लगभग ५०० मजदूर सुरंग मे फंसल हेबाक आशंका अछि।

ब्रिगेडियर एस. नेपालके सेनाके प्रवक्ता जनरल राजा राम बस्नेट विदेशी विशेषज्ञके सहयोगमे टोली अनेक जलविद्युत परियोजनामे कार्यरत बतौलनि । सेना द्वारा जारी विजुअल में बचाव दल अन्हार, मलबा स भरल सुरंग में प्रवेश करैत, कीचड़ आ पानि में डुबकी लगाबैत आ चट्टान के ऊपर चढ़ैत देखल गेल अछि, जखन कि ओ जीवन के संकेत खोजैत छल।

चीनी तरफ स॑ बचाव दल न॑ कीचड़ स॑ टकराबै वाला इलाका खास करी क॑ ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह सीमा क्रासिंग के आसपास, जे नष्ट होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

खोज कुत्ता के मदद सं किछ बचावकर्मी चट्टान आओर मलबा के बीच के फाँक के तलाशी लेलखिन्ह जेहि सं जीवन के संकेत मिलत. चीन केरऽ सरकारी अखबार ग्लोबल टाइम्स के अनुसार, अन्य टीम न॑ भारी मशीनरी के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ ग्योरॉंग बंदरगाह जाय वाला एगो बड़ऽ राजमार्ग क॑ खाली करै के कोशिश करलकै, जेकरा स॑ ई उम्मीद छेलै कि आपदा क्षेत्र म॑ पहुँचै के रास्ता साफ होय जैतै ।

राहत अभियान फंसल समुदायक तइक पहुंचय कें लेल विस्तार करयत छै

नेपाली अधिकारीसबके अनुसार अखनधरि ११ हजार ८१४ गोटेके उद्धार भेल अछि । आपातकालीन दल हेलीकॉप्टर आरू अन्य विमान के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ वू इलाका म॑ फंसलऽ समुदाय तलक पहुँची रहलऽ छेलै, जहां बाढ़ आरू भूस्खलन स॑ सड़क आरू पुल नष्ट होय गेलऽ छै ।

मंगलवार क॑ अधिकारियऽ न॑ वू इलाका म॑ बची क॑ निकलै वाला लोगऽ क॑ सहायता दै के कोशिश भी तेज करी देलकै, जहां सड़क आरू अन्य परिवहन मार्ग क॑ नुकसान पहुँचलऽ छै या कटलऽ छै ।

उपग्रहक तस्वीर मे नेपाल-चीन सीमा पर बेडरोक आ ग्लेशियर खसि पड़ल, फेर नदी मे बाढ़ि आबि गेल

चीन के विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता गुओ जियाकुन कहलनि जे, चीन के नेपाल के लेल राहत के दोसर बैच मंगलदिन भेजय के उम्मीद अछि, जाहि मे ड्रोन, डीएनए परीक्षण आ जल शुद्धिकरण उपकरण शामिल अछि। चीनी डीएनए परीक्षण विशेषज्ञ नेपाल के शव के पहचान करय मे सेहो मदद करत ओ कहलनि।

आपदा शुरू होला के बाद स॑ ही बचाव आरू राहत मिशन उड़ाबै वाला हेलीकॉप्टर पायलट बिमल शर्मा न॑ कहलकै कि तिब्बत केरऽ नजदीकी सीमावर्ती शहर तिमुरे म॑ तबाही देखी क॑ ओकरा चौंक गेलै जेकरा क॑ हुनी सालौ स॑ जानत॑ छै ।

ओ कहला जे एहन लागल जेना हम एकदम अलग परिदृश्य पर उड़ि रहल छी।

शर्मा कहलनि जे, हुनका द्वारा बचाओल गेल लोक सं बात करबाक मौका कम भेटल अछि, मुदा हुनकर भाव सं पता चलैत अछि जे एहि आपदा सं हुनका कतेक गहींर असर पड़ल अछि.

ओ कहलनि जे, हुनका लोकनिक आँखि मे दर्द देखबा मे आबि रहल अछि, ई हृदयविदारक अछि।

आपदा के शुरुआत हिमालय के ऊँचाई पर हिमनदी के पतन स॑ भेलै

26 अगस्त के आपदा के शुरुआत हिमालय में ऊँच घटनाक्रम के श्रृंखला सं भेल छल. हिमनदी केरऽ पतन स॑ भारी मात्रा म॑ चट्टान, बर्फ आरू पिघललऽ पानी नीचें घाटी म॑ भेजलऽ गेलै, जेकरा स॑ नीचें के तरफ शक्तिशाली बाढ़ आबी गेलै ।

उपग्रह केरऽ इमेजरी के अध्ययन करै वाला वैज्ञानिकऽ न॑ कहलकै कि ई पतन म॑ हिमालयी क्षेत्र केरऽ एगो ग्लेशियर के नीचें बेडरोक केरऽ विफलता शामिल नजर आबी रहलऽ छै । ई चट्टान केरऽ गिरना एतना शक्तिशाली छेलै कि ५.२ परिमाण के भूकंपीय घटना के रूप म॑ पंजीकृत होय गेलै ।

एकरऽ परिणामस्वरूप पानी आरू मलबा केरऽ उफान तिब्बत आरू नेपाल केरऽ घाटी स॑ बहय वाला नदी म॑ प्रवेश करी क॑ तेजी स॑ बढ़ी गेलै । बाढ़िक पानि घर, भवन, सड़क आ पुल कए बहरा गेल आ थाल-कादो आ चट्टान कए नीचा ल गेल।

नेपालके प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाह विपदा जलवायु परिवर्तनके निवारणके लेल कार्यवाहीके आवश्यकताके उजागर करल बटैलै ।

सोमदिन राति सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट मे शाह कहलनि जे, ई घटना संकेत देलक अछि जे जलवायु परिवर्तन के संग हिमालय क्षेत्र मे हमरा सब के सामने जे जोखिम बढ़ि रहल अछि। "अतः ई क्षेत्र क॑ सतर्क रहना चाहियऽ, आरू साथ ही साथ ई समय आबी गेलऽ छै कि हम्में जलवायु परिवर्तन के वजह स॑ पैदा होय वाला आपदा के मुद्दा क॑ अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय के सामने मजबूती स॑ उठाबै ।"

___ २.

सालिक नई दिल्ली स रिपोर्ट केलनि। बीजिंग केरऽ एसोसिएटेड प्रेस केरऽ पत्रकार ई. एडुआर्डो कास्टिलो, हांगकांग केरऽ कनिस लेउंग आरू नई दिल्ली केरऽ ऐजाज हुसैन न॑ ई रिपोर्ट म॑ योगदान देल॑ छै ।

title: American missing in wake of Nepal floods contacted, Nepali officials tell CBS News - CBS News
description: American missing in wake of Nepal floods contacted, Nepali officials tell CBS News  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
Kathmandu, Nepal — One of the dozens of U.S. nationals missing in the wake of the devastating flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border has been contacted, Nepali government officials confirmed to CBS News on Tuesday.

About 85 Americans were still listed as missing, and word that rescuers have managed to contact one could bring hope to thousands of families around the world desperately waiting for word of loved ones.

CBS News was still working to confirm details of the case, and it was unclear who the U.S. national contacted by Nepali agencies might be, where they were located or what condition they were in.

More than 4,600 people were still believed to be missing and at least 1,050 confirmed dead in Nepal alone as of Tuesday, authorities said. Chinese authorities have confirmed that 16 people were killed in Tibet, and more than 550 remained missing on that sided of the border.

People scout for usable materials from debris after flash floods at Trishuli Center in Nepal's Nuwakot district, Sept. 1, 2026. Arun SANKAR/AFP/Getty

About 600 hydroelectric power plant workers are among the missing in Nepal, believed to be trapped inside several projects in the disaster area, according to the Himalayan nation's prime minister.

Work by search and rescue teams to clear mud-blocked tunnels to reach the workers has continued apace, amid concern that oxygen inside could run out.

It was almost a week ago that a mountainside and glacier collapse in the Himalayas triggered avalanches in Tibet and Nepal, which in turn triggered the devastating flash floods.

Recovery teams have found bodies in riverbeds far downstream. No one in the region can remember the sacred Trishuli River ever swelling higher than it did last week.

Rohit Tamang, 22, has spent his entire life in his home perched above the Trishuli. He told CBS News he watched helplessly when the waters surged last Wednesday, and he's not leaving now, "because my childhood memories are here."

Nepal's foreign minister told CBS News on Tuesday that authorities believe many foreigners may have been hiking in the mountains when the disaster struck, leaving them marooned without communications, but possibly safe.

He was hopeful that, rather than mud and water, more good news could soon come down from the Himalayas.

काठमांडू, नेपाल : नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा पर भेल विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ि के बाद लापता दर्जनों अमेरिकी नागरिक मे सँ एक सँ संपर्क कयल गेल अछि, नेपाली सरकारक अधिकारी मंगलदिन सीबीएस न्यूज केँ पुष्टि केलनि।

लगभग 85 अमेरिकी क॑ अखनी भी लापता के रूप म॑ सूचीबद्ध करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, आरू ई खबर कि बचावकर्ता सिनी स॑ संपर्क करै म॑ सफल होय गेलऽ छै, दुनिया भर के हजारों परिवारऽ लेली आशा पैदा करी सकै छै जे अपनऽ प्रियजनऽ के खबर के बेताब इंतजार करी रहलऽ छै ।

सीबीएस न्यूज एखनहु एहि मामलाक विवरणक पुष्टि करबा मे लागल छल, आ ई स्पष्ट नहि छल जे नेपाली एजेंसी द्वारा संपर्क कयल गेल अमेरिकी नागरिक के भ' सकैत अछि, ओ कतय छथि वा कोन हालत मे छथि.

अखनो 4600 स बेसी लोक के लापता हेबाक आशंका अछि आ मंगलदिन धरि असगर नेपाल मे कम स कम 1050 के मौत के पुष्टि भेल अधिकारी सब कहलनि। चीनी अधिकारी न॑ ई बात के पुष्टि करलकै कि तिब्बत म॑ १६ लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छै, आरू सीमा केरऽ वू तरफ ५५० स॑ भी अधिक लोग लापता छै ।

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला के त्रिशुली केन्द्र मे आकस्मिक बाढ़ के बाद मलबा स उपयोगी सामग्री के लेल लोक स्काउट करैत छथि, 1 सितम्बर 2026. अरुण संकर/एएफपी/गेटी

नेपाल मे लापता मे लगभग 600 जलविद्युत संयंत्रक मजदूर शामिल अछि, जकरा आपदा क्षेत्र मे कतेको परियोजना के भीतर फंसल मानल जा रहल अछि, हिमालय राष्ट्र के प्रधानमंत्री के अनुसार।

मजदूरऽ तक पहुँचै लेली कीचड़ स॑ बंद सुरंगऽ क॑ साफ करै के खोज आरू बचाव टीमऽ के काम तेजी स॑ जारी छै, ई चिंता के बीच कि भीतर के ऑक्सीजन खतम होय सकै छै ।

लगभग एक सप्ताह पहिने के बात छै कि हिमालय में पहाड़ के ढाल आरू ग्लेशियर के गिरला के बाद तिब्बत आरू नेपाल में हिमस्खलन शुरू होय गेलै, जेकरा चलतें विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ के शुरुआत होय गेलै ।

रिकवरी टीम कए नदी क बहुत नीचा नदी क तल मे लाश भेटल अछि। एहि क्षेत्र मे कियो याद नहि क सकैत अछि जे पवित्र त्रिशुली नदी कहियो पिछला सप्ताह स बेसी सूजन भेल छल।

22 वर्षीय रोहित तामांग अपन पूरा जीवन त्रिशूली के ऊपर बैसल अपन घर मे बितेने छथि। ओ सीबीएस न्यूज केँ कहलनि जे ओ पिछला बुध दिन जखन पानि मे उछाल आयल छल तखन ओ लाचार भ' क' देखैत छलाह, आ आब ओ नहि जा रहल छथि, "किएक त' हमर बचपनक याद एतय अछि."

नेपाल केरऽ विदेश मंत्री मंगलवार क॑ सीबीएस न्यूज क॑ बतैलकै कि अधिकारियऽ के मानना ​​छै कि जब॑ आपदा आबी गेलऽ छेलै त॑ बहुत सारा विदेशी पहाड़ म॑ पैदल यात्रा करी रहलऽ हुअ॑ सकै छै, जेकरा चलतें वू बिना संचार के डूबी गेलऽ छै, लेकिन संभवतः सुरक्षित छै ।

हुनका आशा छलनि जे थाल-कादो आ पानि सं बेसी जल्दिये हिमालय सं आओर नीक खबरि उतरि सकैत अछि.

NEW DELHI (AP) — Rescue crews in Nepal are racing against time to find hundreds of missing workers who are feared trapped inside hydropower tunnels damaged by flooding that has killed more than 1,000 people across Nepal and China.

At least 900 workers are missing from hydropower projects, with about 500 believed to be inside tunnels, according to officials and industry representatives.

Other WRAL Top Stories

Access to the tunnels has been hampered by flooding, debris and damaged infrastructure, making it difficult for rescue teams to reach workers.

Rescuers are scouring tunnels filled with debris

Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, a Nepal Army spokesperson, said teams assisted by foreign experts were working at several hydropower projects. Army footage showed rescuers entering dark, debris-filled tunnels, wading through mud and climbing over rocks as they searched for the missing.

Mohan Kumar Dangi, president of the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal, said floods damaged at least 12 hydropower projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts, with a combined capacity of 670 MW. Four were under construction, seven operational and one in testing phase, he said.

Hydropower projects undergo risk assessments and other studies before construction, but called the Aug. 26 flooding “something unimaginable,” Dangi said.

Flood damage is hampering access to tunnels

The biggest challenge for rescuers is reaching them.

Many of Nepal’s hydropower projects are in remote, mountainous areas where steep terrain and narrow roads can make access difficult. Flooding has worsened conditions, damaging roads and limiting routes to some sites.

Rescuers also are facing tunnels that are blocked or damaged.

The floods swept mud, huge rocks and debris into underground passages, collapsing sections and trapping workers. Even where tunnel entrances are accessible, crews must clear large amounts of debris before reaching deeper sections.

Debris is obscuring the locations of workers

Finding the missing workers also has proved difficult.

Filmmaker and drone pilot Manish Maharjan, who has been volunteering with the Nepalese army, said some tunnels were “filled with mud like toothpaste in a tube.” At one hydropower project, he used a drone to search to the end of a tunnel but found no sign of life.

Some workers called for help during early hours after floods, while others who escaped said colleagues remained underground. It was not clear whether rescuers had since made contact with those workers or whether they were still alive.

Experts say the first 72 hours after a disaster can be critical. People trapped underground may survive without food for some time, but limited drinking water and breathable air can quickly become life-threatening.

Nepal’s rescue capacity is being tested

Anil Pokhrel, a disaster risk reduction expert and former head of Nepal’s disaster authority, said the flooding exposed weaknesses in Nepal’s rescue capacity. He said rescuers lost valuable time locating the tunnel’s exact entry point and coordinates and lacked heavy equipment and adequately trained personnel.

“Harsh and remote locations with inclement weather worsened the situation. Also, we didn’t have adequately trained human resources to undertake such operations,” he said.

Nepal has more than a century of experience building tunnels but remains poorly prepared for complex tunnel rescues, Pokhrel said.

“We are focused on tunnel design and construction but are not adequately prepared for rescue operations,” he said.

——

Kafle reported from Kathmandu, Nepal.

नई दिल्ली, मिथिला मिरर: नेपाल आ चीन मे एक हजार सं बेसी लोकक जान गेल बाढ़ि सं क्षतिग्रस्त जलविद्युत सुरंगक भीतर फंसल सैकड़ों लापता मजदूर के खोजय लेल नेपाल मे बचाव दल समय के संग दौड़ लगा रहल अछि.

अधिकारी आ उद्योग प्रतिनिधि क अनुसार जलविद्युत परियोजना स कम स कम 900 मजदूर लापता अछि, जाहि मे करीब 500 मजदूर सुरंग क अंदर हेबाक आशंका अछि।

अन्य WRAL शीर्ष कहानियाँ

बाढ़, मलबा आ क्षतिग्रस्त बुनियादी ढांचा के कारण सुरंग तक पहुंच में बाधा आबि गेल अछि, जाहि सं बचाव टीम के मजदूर तक पहुंचनाय मुश्किल भ गेल अछि.

बचावकर्मी मलबा स भरल सुरंग कए झाड़ू लगा रहल अछि

ब्रिगेडियर एस. नेपाली सेनाके प्रवक्ता जनरल राजा राम बस्नेट विदेशी विशेषज्ञके सहयोगमे टोली अनेक जलविद्युत परियोजनामे कार्यरत बतौलनि । सेना केरऽ फुटेज म॑ देखलऽ गेलऽ छै कि बचावकर्मी अन्हार, मलबा स॑ भरलऽ सुरंगऽ म॑ प्रवेश करी क॑ थाल के बीच स॑ डुबकी लगाय क॑ चट्टानऽ प॑ चढ़ी क॑ लापता लोगऽ के खोज करी रहलऽ छै ।

नेपालके स्वतन्त्र विद्युत उत्पादक संघके अध्यक्ष मोहनकुमार डाङी बाढिसँ रसुवा आ नुवाकोट जिल्लामे कमसँ कम १२ जलविद्युत् परियोजनाके क्षति पहुँचल बतौलनि, जकर संयुक्त क्षमता ६७० मेगावाट अछि । ओ कहला जे चारिटा निर्माणाधीन, सातटा परिचालन आ एकटा परीक्षण चरण मे अछि।

डांगी नँ कहलकै कि जलविद्युत परियोजना सिनी मँ निर्माण सँ पहलौ जोखिम के आकलन आरू अन्य अध्ययन करलौ जाय छै, लेकिन 26 अगस्त क बाढ़ क “कुछ अकल्पनीय” कहलकै ।

बाढ़िक नुकसान सुरंग तक पहुंच मे बाधा पहुंचा रहल अछि

बचावकर्ता के लेल सबस पैघ चुनौती हुनका तक पहुंचनाय अछि.

नेपाल केरऽ बहुत सारा जलविद्युत परियोजना दूरस्थ, पहाड़ी क्षेत्रऽ म॑ छै, जहां खड़ा इलाका आरू संकीर्ण सड़कऽ के कारण पहुँच मुश्किल होय सकै छै । बाढ़ि के कारण हालत खराब भ गेल अछि, सड़क के नुकसान पहुंचल अछि आओर किछ जगह पर मार्ग सीमित भ गेल अछि.

बचावकर्मी के सेहो एहन सुरंग के सामना करय पड़ि रहल अछि जे अवरुद्ध या क्षतिग्रस्त भ गेल अछि.

बाढ़ि थाल, विशाल चट्टान आ मलबा भूमिगत मार्ग मे बह गेल, खंड ढहि गेल आ मजदूर फँसा देलक। जहाँ सुरंग के प्रवेश द्वार सुलभ छै, वहीं भी चालक दल क॑ गहरा खंडऽ प॑ पहुँचै स॑ पहल॑ बड़ऽ मात्रा म॑ मलबा साफ करना छै ।

मलबा मजदूर क स्थान अस्पष्ट क रहल अछि

लापता मजदूर के खोजब सेहो मुश्किल साबित भेल अछि.

नेपाली सेना के साथ स्वयंसेवी कार्यरत फिल्म निर्माता आरू ड्रोन पायलट मनीष महर्जन के कहना छै कि कुछ सुरंग “ट्यूब में टूथपेस्ट के तरह कीचड़ स॑ भरलऽ छै ।” एकटा जलविद्युत परियोजना मे ओ ड्रोन क उपयोग कए सुरंग क अंत तक खोजबा लेल केलथि मुदा जीवन क कोनो निशानी नहि भेटल।

बाढ़ि के बाद भोर मे किछ मजदूर मदद के आह्वान केलखिन्ह, त किछ मजदूर जे भागल छलखिन्ह ओ कहलखिन्ह जे सहयोगी भूमिगत रहि गेल छथिन्ह. ई साफ नै छेलै कि ओकरऽ बाद बचावकर्ता सिनी न॑ वू मजदूरऽ स॑ संपर्क करलकै या वू अभी भी जिंदा छै ।

विशेषज्ञ के कहनाय छनि जे कोनो आपदा के बाद पहिल 72 घंटा गंभीर भ सकैत अछि. जमीन कें नीचा फंसल लोग किच्छू समय तइक बिना भोजन कें जीवित रह सकएय छै, मुदा सीमित पीवय कें पानी आ सांस लेवय वाला हवा जल्दी जानलेवा भ सकएय छै.

नेपाल के बचाव क्षमता के परीक्षण भ रहल अछि

आपदा जोखिम कम करय के विशेषज्ञ आ नेपाल के आपदा प्राधिकरण के पूर्व प्रमुख अनिल पोखरेल के कहनाय छनि जे बाढ़ि सं नेपाल के बचाव क्षमता मे कमजोरी के उजागर भेल अछि. हुनी कहलकै कि सुरंग केरौ सटीक प्रवेश बिंदु आरू निर्देशांक के पता लगाबै मँ बचावकर्मी सिनी क बहुमूल्य समय गंवाय देलकै आरू भारी उपकरण आरू पर्याप्त प्रशिक्षित कर्मी के कमी छै ।

ओ कहला जे खराब मौसम क संग कठोर आ दूरस्थ स्थान पर स्थिति आओर खराब भ गेल, संगहि हमरा सब लग एहन ऑपरेशन करबा लेल पर्याप्त प्रशिक्षित मानव संसाधन नहि छल।

नेपाल मे सुरंग बनेबाक एक सदी स बेसी अनुभव अछि, मुदा जटिल सुरंग बचाव क लेल ओ खराब तैयारी मे अछि, पोखरेल कहला।

ओ कहला जे हम सुरंग क डिजाइन आ निर्माण पर ध्यान केंद्रित करि रहल छी, मुदा बचाव कार्य लेल पर्याप्त तैयारी नहि छी।

——
